title: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than the pyramids

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramids.
beats.visual: Timeline shoots across the screen: pyramid left, rocket right, Cleopatra in between

beats.speaker: a
beats.visual: Berlin bust of Cleopatra slides in from the edge; Alexandria pin on a sketch map of Egypt

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; Cleopatra next to pyramids with a question mark

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: No. Khufu's Great Pyramid rose around 2560 BC. But there was a problem: it was already ancient.
beats.visual: David Roberts' 1839 Giza painting; label 'Khufu, c. 2560 BC'

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Pyramid to Cleopatra: about 2,500 years. Cleopatra to Apollo 11 in 1969: about 2,000.
beats.visual: Timeline ruler: bracket '≈2,500 years', bracket '≈2,000 years', NASA bootprint at the far end

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Exactly. Closer to Armstrong's first step than the pyramid's first stone. To her, it was older than she is to us.
beats.visual: Brackets compared side by side; Cleopatra marker slides toward the rocket end

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It still stands at Giza today, the last ancient Wonder.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Cleopatra, closer to the Moon than the pyramids. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Rocket icon flies past the pyramid; History Sketches corner logo

description: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC, Cleopatra died in 30 BC, and Apollo 11 landed in 1969. That puts her about 2,500 years after the pyramid and about 2,000 years before the Moon landing. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #cleopatra #ancientegypt
